cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to all in Rome who are loved by God (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a chain that had me HOPPING on my gold base, from God's calling all the way to glory (Romans 8:30). Now Paul stops and asks, "What then shall we say in response to these things?"

cards.question: Paul's next line starts with "If God is for us…" and ends with a question. What's his point?

answers.text: No one can stand against us
We must earn His help first

cards.text: Then Paul looks at what God has already done. God did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all.

cards.question: God already gave up His own Son for us all. So what does Paul say God will also do?

answers.text: Ask us to pay Him back
Hold back the rest for now

cards.text: Friend, if somebody hands you the keys to the WHOLE bakery, you don't stand there sweating about one sprinkle. Then Paul asks, "Who will bring any charge against God’s elect?"

cards.question: Who will bring any charge against God's elect? Paul answers that it is God who ___.

cards.text: Next Paul asks, "Who is there to condemn us?" He points to Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, and is at the right hand of God.

cards.question: True or false: Paul points to Christ Jesus as the one who will condemn us.

cards.text: Paul says that same Christ Jesus, right there at God's right hand, is interceding for us. For US, friend.
Now Paul asks the big one: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" Then he names trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword.

cards.question: Paul lists trouble, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger and sword. What kind of things are on that list?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Scriptures (Psalm 44:22): "For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered." That's a heavy one, friend.

cards.question: True or false: after that whole list, Paul says trouble, famine or sword can separate us from the love of Christ.
In all those hard things, what does Paul say we are through Him who loved us?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers…" and he's STILL not done. I lose count naming my own six toppings, and this man is covering angels, powers and the FUTURE.

cards.question: Paul adds height and depth, then "anything else in all creation." How much of creation does he say can separate us from the love of God?
True or false: Paul ends by saying this love of God is found in Christ Jesus our Lord.
